# Vendor data

## Quran text (Tanzil Project)

The two XML files were downloaded directly from [Tanzil Project](https://tanzil.net/download/) on 26 September 2026. Both are Tanzil Quran Text release 1.1, narration of Hafs from Asim, Kufi verse count (114 suras, 6236 verses).

| File | Tanzil text type | Used in Amanah for |
|---|---|---|
| `quran-simple-clean.xml` | **Simple Clean**: modern spelling, no diacritics, no pause marks. Tanzil intends it for search, not for display. | Exact matching of submitted text without diacritics, glossary term detection, mapping model spans to canonical words. |
| `quran-uthmani.xml` | **Uthmani**: Uthmani script with full diacritics. | The trusted source text: resolved on the server from the ayah reference the user picks, shown on every screen (verse picker, evidence excerpt, result and review screens), stored with each check, and sent to the AMANAH ML model as `source_ar`. Also exact matching of an Arabic text with diacritics sent by an API client. |

Do not call the Simple Clean text "Uthmani" or "the Mushaf text": it is a search text in modern spelling. The text shown to reviewers as the Quran is always the Uthmani text, and the evidence title reads «نص القرآن الكريم · مشروع Tanzil 1.1 · رواية حفص · الرسم العثماني».

Tanzil Quran Text Copyright (C) 2007-2026 Tanzil Project. License: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0. Verbatim copies may be distributed with attribution and a link to Tanzil; the Quran text must not be changed. The original XML files keep Tanzil's complete copyright notice, and `quran-corpus.json` reproduces it in full (`licenseNotice`), as the notice requires for derived files. See [Tanzil's text license](https://tanzil.net/docs/Text_License) and [updates](https://tanzil.net/updates/).

### `quran-corpus.json`

A positional index generated by `scripts/build-quran-corpus.py`. Each verse string is copied verbatim from the `text` attribute of its `aya` element. The basmala that opens a sura is kept by Tanzil in a separate `bismillah` attribute, so it is never part of verse 1 (except in Al-Fatiha, where it is verse 1). It is copied verbatim into the sura record's `bismillah` (absent for suras 1 and 9); suras 95 and 97 spell it «بِّسْمِ» with a shadda. Amanah prepends it only to the `source_ar` sent to the AMANAH ML model for verse 1, because the team's reference store is Tanzil's plain-text export, where verse 1 begins with it.

Top-level keys:

| Key | Content |
|---|---|
| `attribution` | Short Tanzil credit line. |
| `source` | Project, release and download page. |
| `license` | CC BY 3.0 notice with the verbatim-copy and attribution conditions. |
| `licenseUrl` | `https://tanzil.net/docs/Text_License` |
| `updatesUrl` | `https://tanzil.net/updates/` |
| `version` | `1.1` |
| `verseNumbering` | Kufi count and how the opening basmala is handled. |
| `licenseNotice` | Tanzil's complete copyright block for `simple` and `uthmani`, line for line from the XML header, with only the leading `#` comment markers removed. |
| `textTypes` | For `simple` and `uthmani`: the full Tanzil name, source file, title, narration and how Amanah uses it. |
| `suras` | 114 records `{number, name, simple[], uthmani[], bismillah?}`; `bismillah` is `{simple, uthmani}` from Tanzil's attribute of verse 1. |

Regenerate with:

```bash
python scripts/build-quran-corpus.py
```

The script stops if an XML header does not name Tanzil Quran Text version 1.1 under CC BY 3.0 with the «CHANGING IT IS NOT ALLOWED» notice, if the two files differ in sura or verse layout, or if any sura other than 1 and 9 lacks the separate opening basmala. `tests/quran-source.test.mjs` checks that every verse, every `bismillah` and both `licenseNotice` blocks in the JSON equal the XML.

### How submitted text is matched

The web form never sends Arabic text: the user picks a sura and ayah (or types a reference such as `2:256`), and the server takes the verse from this corpus. The rules below apply only when an API client also sends `originalText`, which must then match that verse.

The bundled text is never modified. Matching works on a temporary copy of the submitted text and of the reference verse:

- Ignored: spaces, punctuation, verse numbers and their decorations (﴿ ﴾ ( ) [ ] and U+06DD), tatweel, Tanzil pause marks, and invisible format characters. Both sides are normalized to NFC.
- Text without diacritics matches only if it equals the **Simple Clean** verse letter for letter. Hamza seats, alef forms, ya and ta marbuta are not unified.
- Text with diacritics matches only if it equals the **Uthmani** verse, diacritics included.
- Anything else is `ABSTAIN`. The note says whether letters or diacritics differ, lists up to five changed words, names another verse when the text matches one exactly, and explains a basmala added before verse 1.

Source links in results point to Tanzil's verse deep link (`https://tanzil.net/#{sura}:{ayah}`). The verse API also returns a second verified link to the same verse with Ibn Kathir's tafsir on the King Saud University electronic Mushaf (`https://quran.ksu.edu.sa/tafseer/katheer/sura{s}-aya{a}.html`).

## Glossary (`glossary.json`)

The ten example terms of the approved glossary on page 8 of the challenge reference pack («المرجعية والحزمة العلمية — نماذج لقاموس المصطلحات الأساسية»): الإسلام، التوحيد، العبادة، النبوة، الوحي، الشريعة، الحديث، السنة، الفتوى، الدعوة. Each term has its approved English equivalents and usage rule as written in the PDF, and the reference [islamic-content.com/dictionary](https://islamic-content.com/dictionary). The file was written by hand from the PDF; nothing was scraped from the dictionary site, and terms beyond these ten need permission from its publisher.

- `detectors[].arabic` are regular expressions over the letters-only Simple Clean text (diacritics and tatweel removed, أ إ آ ٱ written ا). Each pattern must cover whole words.
- `scope` is `quran`, `other` (tafsir and other texts; hadith and tafsir checks are currently removed from the product, so only `quran` and `all` apply to new checks) or `all`. In the Quran, «حديث» means speech and «دعوة» means supplication, so those two terms are only detected outside the Quran.
- `alert` holds an English pattern only where the PDF rule names the reduction (for example التوحيد as unity or monotheism without Tawhid, الوحي as inspiration, الشريعة as criminal law or punishment, العبادة as rites only). `unless` cancels the alert when an approved rendering is present.
- Alerts are checked for English translations only. They are advisory: they never change the model decision, severity or drifts. When a result has an alert, approving it requires the reviewer to confirm the terminology.

`lib/server/glossary.ts` reads this file; `tests/glossary.test.mjs` checks every alert and sweeps the whole Quran with a neutral translation (zero alerts expected).
